content:
**Visual observations from test image:**
- Soybean stem split longitudinally, showing internal pith
- Left (upper stem): white/cream intact pith tissue
- Right (crown/root area): extensive dark brown-to-black discoloration with what appears to be small black bodies (microsclerotia)
- Root system appears dark and deteriorated

**Key candidates:**
- **Charcoal Rot**: gray-to-black internal stem discoloration, numerous tiny black microsclerotia in pith, silver/gray stem cortex
- **Brown Stem Rot**: brown pith discoloration progressing upward from crown, pith intact but brown

**Comparison with Charcoal Rot reference:**
The reference images show split stems with silvery-gray internal discoloration and dark crown/root tissue — very consistent with the test image. The test image shows the characteristic pattern of white upper pith transitioning to heavily blackened tissue near the crown with visible dark sclerotia-like bodies.
